s: A company has 200 accounts in AWS Organizations and adds about 10 new accounts each month. The security team works from a dedicated security-tooling account. It must enable Amazon GuardDuty and AWS Security Hub CSPM in every account and every enabled Region, automatically cover new accounts, manage settings centrally, and view all findings in one place. The security team must not use the management account for daily operations. Which solution meets these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?
o: From the management account, designate the security-tooling account as the delegated administrator for GuardDuty (in each enabled Region) and for Security Hub CSPM. From the security-tooling account, turn on auto-enable for all organization members in GuardDuty in each Region, and use Security Hub CSPM central configuration with a home Region and cross-Region aggregation.
From the security-tooling account, send GuardDuty and Security Hub CSPM member invitations to every account in every Region and accept them with a Lambda function in each account.
Use CloudFormation StackSets from the management account to enable GuardDuty and Security Hub CSPM in each account, keeping the management account as the administrator for both services.
Enable GuardDuty and Security Hub CSPM independently in each account, and use Amazon EventBridge rules to forward all findings to an event bus in the security-tooling account.

w.y: With a delegated administrator, the security account manages both services organization-wide without the management account. GuardDuty auto-enable and Security Hub CSPM central configuration cover new accounts and all Regions automatically, and aggregation gives one view of findings.

o.A: Correct: delegated administrator plus auto-enable and central configuration gives automatic, centralized coverage.
o.B: Invitation-based membership is a legacy, manual approach for accounts outside an organization and does not scale.
o.C: This makes the management account the operating administrator, which the requirement forbids, and StackSets add upkeep.
o.D: Settings in each account stay unmanaged, and new accounts are not enabled automatically. This only forwards findings.

d: auto-cover new accounts, not management account, LEAST operational overhead
